suggestions: reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
SELECT cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, count(*) cnt1, cd_purchase_estimate, count(*) cnt2, cd_credit_rating, count(*) cnt3
FROM (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk AS customer_sk, c.c_current_cdemo_sk AS cdemo_sk
    FROM customer c
    JOIN customer_address ca ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
    WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('IL','TX','ME')
      AND exists (select * from store_sales,date_dim where c.c_customer_sk = ss_customer_sk and ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year = 2002 and d_moy between 1 and 1+2)
      AND (not exists (select * from web_sales,date_dim where c.c_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk and ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year = 2002 and d_moy between 1 and 1+2) and not exists (select * from catalog_sales,date_dim where c.c_customer_sk = cs_ship_customer_sk and cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year = 2002 and d_moy between 1 and 1+2))
) AS filtered_customers
JOIN customer_demographics ON cd_demo_sk = filtered_customers.cdemo_sk
GROUP BY cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
ORDER BY cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
LIMIT 100
